title: The Cherokee date for an independent label after the Decca falling-out
summary: After fighting with Decca's Dave Kapp, Barnet recorded Cherokee, Redskin Rhumba and others for a short-lived label whose name he cannot recall.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What year was that?
The film --
That was '43, that's right.
The film was '44.

Oh, '44, yeah. '43 and '44. No, there wasn't any recording strike. We recorded -- oh, I know what was wrong. I got into a fight with -- it was with Decca, and I got in a fight with Dave Kapp and we mutually agreed to sever all connections. That was -- and I was not with any record company at the time. I think we did make one date for an independent guy. I couldn't even tell you the label. It might have been -- no, it wasn't Atlantic. It was an ill fated venture, because the company never happened. I think they were on that date. But what we did then, we did, "Cherokee", again, and in other words they were free to do it, it had been long enough, you know. And we did, "Cherokee," and, "The Redskin Rhumba," and -- "Atlantic Jump", we did too. And, "Bunny." I can't think of the name of the record company. It was ill fated.
Did they ever release the record? The record company didn't last, but I mean did the records ever get out?
Yes, yes.
That would be interesting to know on what label that they got out. Great to hear. The next
listing is --
You know, I've never -- Pat, I've never seen that record date listed in any discography. It's very strange.
Do you know for sure the records got out?
Well, I know, 'Cherokee,' did. But see, we did, 'Bunny,' and the other one again, later, and it's a little confusing.
Do you think the name of the company might come to you later as we talk?
No way. No way.
You've totally forgotten, huh? Gee, that would really be something to hear. Those could be very special kinds of collector's items, you know?
Well, they could be if both those guys are on there, and I'm pretty sure they were. But they -- there's just no way I'd ever remember the name of the company.
Any chance Chubby would?
He might. Although you might get a bunch of monumental misinformation.
He might tell me that Oscar just wasn't making it, right?
Well --
